- **Luna** is the fastest, but it got the lede by replacing three whole paragraphs in one edit. In the editor that's one big red block and one big green block, which is close to the "rewrite the whole doc" we're trying to avoid. It also left "Mistakes were made" alone in both runs.
- **Sonnet** did each task with small, readable edits. On the launch update it rewrote the opening sentence to lead with the news, then removed the repeated announcement from paragraph 3. Its notes match its edits. It also saw that the memo's proposal was buried and led with it, which no check asked for.

**I'd pick Sonnet 5.5.** It was the only one that got the structural fix right without turning it into a near-rewrite. Visible, granular diffs are what the brief judges ("are diffs clear and useful?"). The cost is about 1.3 s more per request than Haiku (4.2 s vs 2.9 s), which the thinking shimmer covers. At about $0.007 a call, the remaining ~$4.97 is roughly 700 requests, far more than reviewers will use.

If speed has to win, Haiku is the better fallback: its ⌘K edits are as good as Sonnet's and it's 1 s faster. It's weak at whole-doc structure, which is exactly what the Review doc button exists for.

This is one run per case, so read latency differences of under a second as rough.

The default model is still Haiku until you decide. Nothing is committed yet: the changes and the new report (`eval/reports/2026-11-01-17-54-haiku-luna-sonnet.md`) are in the working tree. Say the word and I'll set the default and commit.

Everything is wired, tested and committed except `.env.example`, which you said you'll edit. These are the lines to paste in under `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=`:

```
# Optional. Review doc (whole document, needs judgment):
OPENROUTER_MODEL_REVIEW=anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5
# Optional. ⌘K and refine (small scoped edits, speed matters):
OPENROUTER_MODEL_EDIT=anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5
```

Tell me when it's saved and I'll commit it. The code already falls back to those two models when the variables aren't set.

**Wiring:** Review doc goes to Sonnet 5.5; ⌘K and refine go to Haiku 5.5. In the browser, the editor records your edits while each request runs, so suggestions land on the right text when they arrive, and any whose text you changed are dropped and reported. The doc autosaves locally, and Review doc and ⌘K both have Cancel.

**Results**, full output above:
- **`npm test`:** 38 passed. That's spec tests 1–20 plus extra edge cases.
- **`npm run test:e2e`:** 12 passed, spec tests 21–32. The tests' server has an invalid key, so a test can never spend money.
- **`npm run build`:** clean, with `/api/suggest` in the build.

**Test changes:** test 20's wording changed because you replaced `OPENROUTER_MODEL` with two variables. The new version is stricter: it checks that all three request types reach the right model. No test was loosened.

To check the tests can fail, I disabled the edit tracking: test 28, the "type while it's thinking" test, failed as it should. Test 29 still passed, correctly, because the quote re-check catches that case independently.

**The real run cost $0.0245 of the $0.10**, read from `/key`. It matches the per-call total of $0.0247. About $4.94 is left.

The final run did everything you asked:
- Review doc gave 2 suggestions.
- I accepted one and rejected one.
- Since the review gave only 2, ⌘K produced a suggestion to refine.
- I refined it twice ("shorter", then "more formal").
- I typed " (draft)" into the title while a ⌘K request was running. The answer still landed correctly, 8 characters further on, and the typed text was kept.

**What the run caught, and what I fixed:**
- **Refine broke sentences.** The "more formal" version would have accepted as "In In the first week". Marking the span in the prompt only turned that into "In during…". The real cause was that refine asked the model to rewrite a fragment starting mid-phrase. The server now widens the span to whole sentences and trims the result back to a small diff. Three live retries all read correctly, and the final run shows "During the first week, …".
- **Cursor under the top bar:** typing near the top could leave the cursor hidden. Fixed with scroll margins.
- **Whole-doc review:** it no longer greys out the entire document while it runs.
- **Stale note:** the review's note now clears once every suggestion is handled.

One page-jump I chased turned out to be my script clicking mid-animation; at a human pace, nothing scrolls.

**Still open:** Haiku's ⌘K notes sometimes overstate. One said it "merged" a sentence when it only cut two phrases.

The walkthrough screenshots are in `/Users/thomaslrgregoriogmail.com/Developer/chiri-editor/design/screenshots/live/` (git-ignored); `07-refined-2.png` and `09-after-typing.png` show the final state.

  ## Findings: chiri-editor review
  
  I found no critical bugs. I proved the two ⌘K popover bugs (findings 1 and 2) with throwaway Playwright tests in a scratch clone. Everything else below comes from reading the code or running small snippets. The real repo is untouched (`git status` is clean). The scratch clone is at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-thomaslrgregoriogmail-com-Developer-chiri-editor/9d4e72df-c41f-48e9-9326-e3b587a0a107/scratchpad/clone, with the probes in `tests/e2e/zz-probe.spec.ts`.
  
  ### 1. "Try again" after a ⌘K error sends the old, unmoved scope
  - **Severity:** medium
  - **Where:** `components/Workspace.tsx:221`, with `AskPopover.tsx:82`
  - **What goes wrong:** The first submit clears `askTarget`. After that, nothing moves the target when the user types. Retry falls back to `ask.target`, which still holds the range from the first submit.
  - **Steps:** Doc is `"Intro.\n\nThe quick brown fox."`. Press ⌘K on the fox paragraph and pick Tighten. While it's thinking, click into the editor and type `"Hello world. "` at the start (typing during a request is meant to work). The request fails with a 502 or 504. Click Try again.
  - **Result:** The retry sends scope `{8,28}`, which now covers `"rld. Intro.\n\nThe qui"`. Suggestions can land in the wrong paragraph, the shimmer covers the wrong range, and if the user deleted text the request gets a 400 "scope is outside the document".
  - **Confidence:** verified (probe P1).
  - **Fix:** Keep the target moving after submit (keep it in the field or map it through `req.changes()`), or map `ask.target` on retry.
  
  ### 2. ⌘K while an earlier ⌘K is still thinking: the old answer takes over the new popover
  - **Severity:** medium
  - **Where:** `Workspace.tsx:196-208` (`openAsk` doesn't check `ask.phase`), `Workspace.tsx:228-233`
  - **What goes wrong:** Click-outside is turned off while thinking, so the user can click into the editor and press ⌘K on another paragraph. `openAsk` replaces `ask` but never cancels the running request, and that request's id is lost.
  - **Result:** When the old answer arrives, `setAsk(null)` closes the new popover (if suggestions were added), or `setAsk(a => …phase:"done")` swaps the new popover's half-typed instruction for the old answer's message.
  - **Confidence:** verified (probe P2). After the old reply, the new popover showed "Old answer: reads well. Close" and the textbox was gone.
  - **Fix:** In `openAsk`, cancel the running request (or refuse to reopen while thinking). In `submitAsk`, ignore the result unless `askRequestRef.current === req.id`.
  
  ### 3. Cancel or a non-JSON 200 can surface as "Cannot read properties of null"
  - **Severity:** low
  - **Where:** `lib/client/api.ts:11-13`
  - **What goes wrong:** `res.json().catch(() => null)` also swallows an AbortError raised while the body is still downloading. With `res.ok` true it returns `null`, and `placeSuggestions` then throws a TypeError.
  - **Result:** After a Cancel that lands in that window (or a 200 with an HTML body), the status bar shows an error instead of staying quiet.
  - **Confidence:** traced in code. The window is small.
  - **Fix:** If `res.ok` and the JSON is null, throw; also rethrow AbortError from the `.catch`.
  
  ### 4. A refine that touches another suggestion in the same sentence is thrown away with a misleading message
  - **Severity:** low
  - **Where:** `lib/server/suggest.ts:90-117`, `lib/editor/place.ts:44`, `Workspace.tsx:282-284`
  - **What goes wrong:** The server widens the refine to whole sentences. If a second suggestion B sits in that sentence and the model's rewrite reaches B's words, the new range overlaps B. `placeSuggestions` counts it as stale.
  - **Result:** The user sees "The text changed while refining. Kept the original." but nothing changed, and the model call was paid for.
  - **Confidence:** traced in code.
  - **Fix:** Tell this case apart and say so ("overlaps another suggestion"), or send the other suggestions' ranges as off-limits.
  
  ### 5. A fresh clone has no README, and the Playwright browser install isn't documented
  - **Severity:** medium (reviewer experience)
  - **Where:** repo root. SPEC §9 promises a README.
  - **What goes wrong:** Nothing tells a reviewer to `npm ci`, copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in the key, or run `npx playwright install chromium`. `npm run test:e2e` fails on a machine with no browsers installed.
  - **Other notes:**
    - CLAUDE.md still says `npm run dev` shows "the design mock; `?state=ask`", which is stale.
    - There is no `engines` field or `.nvmrc`. On Node older than 20.12, `process.loadEnvFile` is missing; the try/catch hides that, and eval/credit then report "OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not set".
  - **Confidence:** verified. The clean clone needs these steps. Everything else in the clean clone passed (see the checked list).
  - **Fix:** Add a README with setup steps and the Playwright install, and add `"engines": {"node": ">=20.12"}`.
  
  ### 6. Trimming can split a decomposed accent from its letter
  - **Severity:** low
  - **Where:** `lib/server/locate.ts:77-83`
  - **What goes wrong:** `isWord` doesn't treat combining marks (`\p{M}`) as part of a word.
  - **Result:** Quote `"é x"` with replacement `"è x"` trims to a delete of a lone U+0301 and an insert of a lone U+0300. The diff renders as a floating accent with a strikethrough. Text pasted from macOS or PDFs is often decomposed like this.
  - **Confidence:** verified by running `sharedEnds` in vitest.
  - **Fix:** Add `\p{M}` to the `isWord` character class.
  
  ### 7. The server and client disagree on whether touching edits overlap
  - **Severity:** low
  - **Where:** `locate.ts:48` vs `place.ts:12`
  - **What goes wrong:** The server only drops edits whose untrimmed ranges overlap. After trimming, edit 1 can become an insertion at position p while edit 2's trimmed range starts at p (e.g. `"abc"→"abc x"` and `" def"→"!def"`). The client's `conflicts()` treats an insertion on an edge as a conflict.
  - **Result:** The second edit is silently counted as "couldn't be placed".
  - **Confidence:** traced, with a partial run.
  - **Fix:** Run the client's rule (insertion on an edge = overlap) on the trimmed ranges in `locateEdits`, so the server reports `overlap`.
  
  ### 8. Small items (nits)
  - **Empty ⌘K target can be sent:** `submitAsk` (`Workspace.tsx:221`) doesn't recheck for an empty target. If the user deletes the target paragraph while the popover is open, it sends an empty scope and gets back a confusing "couldn't be placed".
  - **Refine inputs have no size limit:** In refine mode, `target.replacement` and `history[*]` (`schema.ts:24-25`) have no max length, unlike `doc`. A client could send large prompts. It's a local app, so this is minor; add `.max(MAX_DOC_CHARS)`.
  - **Dry-run reports land in a tracked folder:** `npm run eval -- --dry-run` writes `eval/reports/*-dry.md` into the tracked reports folder, so it's easy to commit by accident. Ignore `*-dry.md` or write them somewhere else.
  
  ### Checked and found fine
  - **Placement and offsets:**
    - `locateEdits` handles uniqueness (including overlapping matches), `outside_scope`, `noop` and the empty quote. Offsets are UTF-16, and the surrogate-pair guard in `sharedEnds` works.
    - The trimmed quote always equals `doc.slice(from, to)`.
    - `sentencesAround` behaves on "v2.0", "!", "?", the end of the doc, and an insertion at the end of a paragraph (the trimmed refine landed correctly).
    - `paragraphAround` is fine apart from a theoretical blank-line edge case.
  - **Mapping and accept:**
    - `changeTouches`/`mapRange`/`mapSuggestion`: typing at an edge shifts the range, typing inside drops the suggestion, and the re-check against `quote` holds.
    - `acceptSuggestion` and `acceptAll` use pre-change coordinates on non-overlapping ranges.
    - Undo works through CM history.
    - Each request in flight builds its own composed set of edits (`Pending.changes` composed in the update listener); there's no gap between the response arriving and the suggestions being placed.
    - Refine replaces the original only if it's still there, and keeps the original when it can't place the new one.
  - **API key:**
    - It isn't in the client bundle (grepped `.next/static` after `next build`).
    - It's redacted in provider errors and never part of the error message (`SuggestError`).
    - The route logs only `e.message`.
    - Eval and credit print only money fields.
    - No real `sk-or-` key appears in git history (only the fake key in the tests).
    - `.env*` is ignored except `.env.example`.
    - `window.__view` is exposed in dev builds only.
    - The e2e tests use an invalid key, and `reuseExistingServer` is false.

content.text:
The reviewer found **no critical bugs** and nothing that leaks the key. Every finding is real. I checked the important ones against the code myself, and the repo is untouched. Nothing is fixed yet.

**Your main worry, suggestions landing on the wrong text, didn't happen in any finding.** Every suggestion is re-checked against its exact quoted text before it's shown, so it can't land on changed words. The worst case below is the AI being pointed at the wrong passage.

**Ranked, worst first:**

1. **⌘K opened while an earlier ⌘K is still thinking.** (Medium. The reviewer reproduced it, and I confirmed it in the code: `components/Workspace.tsx:196` and `:228-236`.)
   - What happens: you click away from a thinking popover and press ⌘K on another paragraph. When the first answer arrives, it closes the new popover, or overwrites your half-typed instruction with the old answer's message.
   - Cause: opening ⌘K never cancels the request already running, and the answer handler doesn't check which popover it belongs to.
   - Fix: cancel the running request when ⌘K reopens, and ignore answers whose request ID isn't the current one.

2. **"Try again" after a ⌘K error sends the old position.** (Medium. Reproduced, and confirmed at `Workspace.tsx:221` and `:224`.)
   - What happens: if you typed above the paragraph while the first try was running, the retry points at shifted text, for example "rld. Intro…The qui". The AI then edits the wrong stretch of text and the shimmer covers the wrong range. If you had deleted text, the retry fails with an error instead.
   - Cause: after the first submit, nothing keeps the target's position in step with your edits.
   - Fix: map the target through the edits made since, before retrying.

3. **A fresh clone has no setup instructions.** (Medium for the reviewer experience. The reviewer confirmed it on a clean clone.)
   - What's missing: no README saying to run `npm ci`, copy `.env.example` to `.env`, and install the test browser with `npx playwright install chromium`. Without that browser, `npm run test:e2e` fails.
   - Also: CLAUDE.md line 7 still calls the app "the design mock", which I confirmed is stale. And nothing pins the Node version: on Node older than 20.12, the eval and credit scripts wrongly report the key as missing.
   - Fix: write the README, which is the next task anyway, and add `"engines": {"node": ">=20.12"}`.

4. **A cancel at the wrong moment can show a TypeError.** (Low. Found by reading the code; I confirmed `lib/client/api.ts:11`.)
   - What happens: in a narrow window, a cancelled request (or a successful response whose body isn't JSON) is treated as an empty answer. The status line then shows "Cannot read properties of null" instead of staying quiet.
   - Fix: don't swallow cancellation while reading the response, and throw if a successful response has no data.

5. **Refine discards a valid rewrite with a misleading message.** (Low. Found by reading the code.)
   - What happens: refine widens to whole sentences. If another suggestion sits in the same sentence and the rewrite touches its words, the new version is thrown away. The message then says "The text changed while refining", which is untrue, and you've paid for the call.
   - Fix: give that case its own honest message, or tell the model which spans are off-limits.

6. **Server and client disagree on edits that touch end to end.** (Low. Found by reading the code, partly tested.)
   - What happens: after trimming, one edit can become an insertion right where another starts. The server keeps both; the client then silently drops the second as "couldn't be placed", where it should have been reported as an overlap.
   - Fix: apply the client's overlap rule on the trimmed ranges in `locateEdits`.

7. **Accents typed as a separate character can be split.** (Low. The reviewer ran it, and I confirmed `lib/server/locate.ts:77` doesn't count accent marks as part of a word.)
   - What happens: text pasted from macOS or PDFs often stores "é" as "e" plus a separate accent character. Trimming can then split them, so the diff strikes out a floating accent on its own.
   - Fix: count combining marks as part of a word.

8. **Nits:**
   - If you delete the target paragraph while the ⌘K box is open, it still sends an empty range.
   - Refine accepts its replacement and history fields with no size limit.
   - `eval --dry-run` reports land in the tracked reports folder, so they're easy to commit by accident.

**Covered and fine:**
- **Key:** not in the client bundle (the reviewer searched the production build), redacted from errors, not in git history, and only money fields are printed.
- **Placement and offsets:** emoji, overlap rules, sentence widening.
- **Mapping:** typing at an edge shifts a suggestion, typing inside drops it, and every concurrent request keeps its own record of edits.
- **Editor actions:** accept, accept all, undo, the two cancel paths and the keymap.
- **Clean clone on Node 24:** install, typecheck, 38 unit tests, the dry-run eval, the build and all 12 e2e tests pass.

I'd fix 1, 2 and 4 together, since they're all in the request lifecycle, then 6 and 7, and cover 3 with the README. 5 and the nits can wait or go in the README's "with more time" section.

content.text:
All the review findings and nits are fixed. Every bug fix has a test that failed before the fix and passes now, and all three runs are green on a clean tree.

**Fail → pass, one line each:**

| Finding | Test | Before the fix | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. ⌘K while another is thinking | R1 (e2e) | the old answer replaced the new popover, and the half-typed instruction was gone | ✓, and the old request is cancelled |
| 2. "Try again" sends a stale range | R2 (e2e) | the retry sent the old range | ✓ sends where the paragraph is now |
| 4. A cancel shows a TypeError | R4a, R4b (unit) | the client returned `null` for a cancel mid-download and for a non-JSON reply | ✓ throws the cancel and a readable error |
| 5. Refine's message | R5 (e2e) | "The text changed while refining" | ✓ "The new version overlaps another suggestion, so it wasn't applied" |
| 6. Server/client disagree on touching edits | R6 (unit) | the server kept both edits | ✓ drops the second as overlap, using one rule shared with the client |
| 7. Decomposed accents | R7 (unit) | trimmed down to a lone accent mark | ✓ keeps "café" whole |
| Nit: empty target | R-nit (e2e) | the retry was sent, and the stale range crashed the shimmer with a `RangeError` | ✓ no request; says the paragraph is gone |
| Nit: refine field sizes | R-nit (unit) | a 500 error after reaching the model call | ✓ 400, no model call |

The other nits have no test, since they're configuration:
- Dry-run reports go to `eval/reports/dry/`, which git ignores (checked with `git check-ignore`).
- `package.json` requires Node 20.12 or newer.
- CLAUDE.md no longer calls the app "the design mock".

**Final runs** (output above):
- `npm test`: 43 passed
- `npm run test:e2e`: 16 passed (spec tests 21–32 plus the 4 regression tests)
- `npm run build`: clean

**Commits:**
1. `70246ae` accents
2. `89ff175` touching edits
3. `0cba8d6` API client
4. `f560402` size limits
5. e2e helpers refactor

input.content:
# Draft: a Markdown editor with an AI co-author

![Review doc on the sample document: real Sonnet 5.5 output](docs/screenshot-light.png)

*Review doc on the sample document. This is real model output: two suggestions, shown inline (red struck = removed, green underlined = added), each with its reason in the margin. The document doesn't change until you accept. [Dark mode](docs/screenshot-dark.png).*

## Run it

Needs Node 20.12+ and an OpenRouter key.

```sh
npm ci
cp .env.example .env        # then put your key in OPENROUTER_API_KEY
npm run dev                 # http://localhost:3000
```

The two model variables in `.env.example` are optional; the defaults are the models described below.

Checks:

```sh
npm test                           # unit + API tests, OpenRouter mocked
npx playwright install chromium    # once, for the browser tests
npm run test:e2e                   # browser tests, API intercepted, nothing billed
npm run build
```

`npm run eval -- --dry-run` runs the model eval against a fake model (free). Without `--dry-run` it calls real models and costs money.

## What it does

- **Write Markdown** in a document-style editor. Markdown marks (`#`, `**`, `-`, `>`, backticks, link URLs) are hidden except on the line you're editing. The text underneath is always plain Markdown.
- **Review doc** (top right) reads the whole document and suggests up to five small edits, or none if the text is fine.
- **⌘K** asks about the paragraph under the cursor, or the selection: type an instruction or pick a preset (Tighten, Fix grammar, More formal, More casual, Clarify).
- **Each suggestion** has Accept, Reject and Refine. Refine takes a follow-up ("shorter", "more formal") and remembers earlier rounds.
- **Keep typing while it thinks.** Answers land on the right text even after you've edited above or around it.
- **Keys:** ⌥↵ accepts and Esc rejects when the cursor is inside a suggestion. ⌘Z undoes an accept. Tab still indents.
- The document is saved to your browser (localStorage). The first visit loads a sample document.

## How it works

**Anchoring.** The model never returns the whole document. It returns up to five `{quote, replacement, reason}` edits. The server looks for each quote by exact match. If a quote occurs zero times, or more than once, that edit is dropped and counted ("1 suggestion couldn't be placed"), never guessed. The text the quote and replacement share at the start and end is trimmed off, at word boundaries, so a one-word fix shows as a one-word diff. Offsets are UTF-16, as in JavaScript strings and CodeMirror. Code: `lib/server/locate.ts`.

**Mapping while you type.** Every request remembers the document as it was sent and records every edit made after that. When the answer arrives, each suggestion is moved through those edits (CodeMirror's `ChangeSet.mapPos`). Then it's re-checked: the text at the new position must still equal the quote, or the suggestion is dropped. Suggestions already on screen follow your edits the same way, and disappear if you edit inside them. Code: `lib/editor/mapping.ts`, `lib/editor/place.ts`, `components/Workspace.tsx`.

**Two models.**
- Review doc uses Claude Sonnet 5.5, with reasoning set to `low`, the lowest it accepts. Reviewing a whole document needs judgment: in the eval, Sonnet was the only model that fixed a buried lede with small edits.
- ⌘K and refine use Claude Haiku 5.5, with reasoning off. Those are small, scoped edits, where Haiku was as good and about 1 s faster.

Both are set in `lib/server/models.ts` and can be overridden with `OPENROUTER_MODEL_REVIEW` / `OPENROUTER_MODEL_EDIT`. The API key is only read by the server route (`app/api/suggest/route.ts`), and it's redacted from any error passed back.

**The eval.** `eval/` has three documents with real problems planted in them: a buried lede, a rambling paragraph, passive voice, typos and a vague claim. Each also has a paragraph that's already good, to catch over-editing. Checks are pass/fail, and `eval/reports/` keeps the side-by-side output for every model. All prompt text lives in one file, `lib/prompts.ts`.

**Where to look first.** `SPEC.md` has the decisions and the test list. `DESIGN.md` has the visual system. `CLAUDE.md` has the commands and the non-obvious rules.

## Left out on purpose

- **Auth, a database, real-time collaboration, deployment.** The brief asks for none of them. One person and one document in localStorage is enough to show the editing loop.
- **Fuzzy quote matching.** A suggestion in the wrong place is worse than a missing one, so unplaceable edits are dropped and reported.
- **Streaming.** The answer is a short JSON list; a shimmer on the text being worked on covers the wait.
- **A rendered preview pane.** Live preview (hidden marks) already makes the document read as a document.
- **Rate limiting.** The app runs locally on your own key, and each request is capped (40k characters in, 1200 tokens out).
- **Version history** beyond undo.

## How I used AI to build it

Built with Claude Code. The full sessions are in `ai-sessions/`, unedited except for masked keys.

- **Spec first.** No code until `SPEC.md` was agreed: the decisions, the request/response contract, and the test list. The UI started from `DESIGN.md` and a static mock, which I checked from screenshots in both themes and at phone width before anything was wired up.
- **The eval picked the models.** The first comparison showed Sonnet can't turn reasoning off. After changing two prompts (the note may only describe what the edits do; a buried lede means rewriting the opening), the second run showed what the split should be.
- **Tests as the bar.** Every task ended with `npm test`, `npm run test:e2e` and `npm run build` green. I also deliberately broke the code to make sure the important tests can fail.
- **A real run in the browser**, with a screenshot at every step, found bugs the tests didn't: refine rewriting a fragment into "In In the first week", and the cursor hidden under the top bar. Both are fixed.
- **A fresh review.** A separate agent with no context read the code and found seven issues, including two ⌘K race conditions. Each fix began with a test that failed without it.
- **Guardrails.** A Claude Code deny rule kept the agent from reading the key file, live API spend was capped per task, and every live run was rehearsed with mocks first.

## What it cost

$0.057 of the $5 key, read from OpenRouter's `/api/v1/key`:
- two model-comparison runs: $0.002, then $0.030
- browser walkthroughs and refine checks: $0.025

Development and all tests run against mocks.

## With more time

- **Refine and neighbouring suggestions.** Refine widens its span to whole sentences, because rewriting trimmed fragments produced broken text. If another suggestion sits in that sentence and the rewrite reaches it, the new version is discarded (and the card says so). Better: tell the model which spans are off-limits, or merge the two suggestions.
- **Word-level diffs inside a replacement**, so text kept in the middle of a rewrite isn't shown as deleted and re-added.
- **Notes that match the edits.** Haiku's one-line notes sometimes describe more than its edits do. Generate the note from the edits that were placed, or check it against them.
- **A bigger eval:** more documents, several runs per case, latency spread rather than one sample.
- **Phone layout:** only the active suggestion's card shows under its paragraph. A bottom sheet would make moving between suggestions easier.

Needs Node 20.12+ and an OpenRouter key.

```sh
npm ci
cp .env.example .env        # then put your key in OPENROUTER_API_KEY
npm run dev                 # http://localhost:3000
```
